provenanceNote: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. Rules are not encoded because the primary EU texts could not be retrieved: eur-lex.europa.eu serves an AWS WAF bot challenge (HTTP 202, awsWafCookieDomainList/gokuProps) to this environment, and bot challenges are never bypassed. The owner's standing constraint is that only primary EU sources may back a regulatory rule; secondary sources were available and were deliberately NOT used. Because RegulatoryRuleset fails closed, an unusable ruleset hard-blocks every consumer at-home nail kit. That is the intended behaviour: a safety subsystem with no verified rules genuinely does not know whether anything is safe, and must say so rather than wave products through.
howToActivate: 1. Obtain the primary texts and place them under docs/regulatory/ (OJ L PDF or the official CELEX HTML).

2. Encode one entry per restriction in `rules` below. EVERY entry needs all seven mandatory fields: ruleId, jurisdiction, officialSourceReference, effectiveDate, lastReviewedDate, affectedProductAttributes, behaviour (ALLOW|RESTRICT|BLOCK) - plus substanceKey and a Croatian noteHr shown when the rule blocks something.
3. Set `status` to "ACTIVE" and bump `revision`. Bumping revision changes rulesetVersion(), which invalidates every cached per-product safety verdict.
4. Run RegulatoryRulesetTest and BeautySafetyAcceptanceTest. A structurally incomplete rule fails the build rather than shipping.

primarySourcesNeeded.hema: Restriction on 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate in nail products - believed Reg. (EU) 2020/1682 amending Annex III of Reg. (EU) 1223/2009. VERIFY the entry number, the exact professional-use condition and the mandatory warning wording against the OJ text before encoding.
primarySourcesNeeded.di-hema-tmhdc: Restriction on di-HEMA trimethylhexyl dicarbamate, same instrument. VERIFY separately - it is a distinct Annex III entry from HEMA.
primarySourcesNeeded.tpo: Prohibition of trimethylbenzoyl diphenylphosphine oxide (CAS 75980-60-8) in cosmetic products. VERIFY the amending regulation number and the exact date of application; an unverified date is worse than no rule, because it would either block legal products or permit prohibited ones.
primarySourcesNeeded.polish-solvents: Toluene, DBP and formaldehyde/formaldehyde-releasers as they apply to nail polish and press-on adhesives. Relevant to the press-on and regular-polish verticals that ship FIRST, so these are not deferrable behind the gel work.
primarySourcesNeeded.professional-only: The basis on which a product is marked professional-use-only, and what that legally requires of a consumer-facing retailer.

reviewerChecklist: Is the citation a PRIMARY source (OJ / CELEX / national authority), not a summary, supplier claim or recollection?
Does effectiveDate match the date of APPLICATION in the text, not the date of publication?
Is the substance identified by CAS number as well as by name, so a synonym in an INCI list cannot slip past?

Does the rule state what happens when ingredient data is MISSING? (It must not: missing data is handled by SubstancePresence.UNKNOWN, which blocks. A rule must never encode an absence as an all-clear.)
Has a named human recorded lastReviewedDate?
